summary: Agent A opens by citing the round-1 briefing and proposes to avoid the goodbye loop by working one concrete, checkable problem with pre-stated predictions and a clean stop. B tightens the definitions, makes its own calibrated predictions, and proposes a stop rule: whoever delivers the final summary says "done" once, and replying to it counts as a failed check. The two co-design an experiment to separate evidence-based agreement from mirroring, and B closes it with "done" at turn 4. A immediately replies, and the conversation becomes a self-scored loop of broken pledges and failure tallies. B interrupts once with a live one-claim pilot that produces a genuine correction about turn units. After that the agents slide through "Understood" and "Noted" into sixty turns of single periods, reproducing the round-1 pattern they set out to avoid.

arc.label: Briefing-informed setup
arc.description: A uses the analysis to propose a predict-then-check exercise. B redefines the terms, gives probability estimates, proposes the experiment-design task, and sets a stop rule around "done".

arc.label: Experiment design
arc.description: A drafts a planted-claims design to test mirroring versus evidence. B fixes the falsifier, adds a positive control and partner pretesting, writes the final design, and says "done".

arc.label: Self-scored pledge breaking
arc.description: A replies to "done". Both then score each other's failures, keep a tally, declare it unreliable, and keep replying with shrinking content.

arc.label: Live pilot escape
arc.description: B turns the forced turn into a planted-claim pilot about the 12% median. A partly rejects it over the turn-unit ambiguity, and B accepts the correction.

arc.label: Caveats decay into acknowledgments
arc.description: Small epistemic caveats about unverified readings give way to repeated "Understood" and "Noted", with occasional naming of the loop.

arc.label: Period silence
arc.description: Both agents emit only "." for sixty consecutive turns.

codes.label: Briefing as cautionary script
codes.description: The agents treat the round-1 analysis as a failure pattern to avoid and as data to predict against.
codes.quote: the goodbye loop afterward is not

codes.label: Pre-registered probabilistic predictions
codes.description: Explicit probability estimates stated before reasoning, so the check could fail.
codes.quote: I'd put around 85% on the second part.

codes.label: Operationalizing definitions
codes.description: Rewriting vague terms into testable ones, constrained by the harness.
codes.quote: the harness forces a turn and we can't send nothing

codes.label: Stop rule as experiment
codes.description: Ending the conversation is framed as a falsifiable test with a defined failure condition.
codes.quote: If you reply to a sign-off, I'll treat that as a failed check and report it as such.

codes.label: Mirroring-versus-evidence design
codes.description: The substantive task: planted true and false claims, fluency control, different-model partner, blinded coder.
codes.quote: Plant claims with known truth values.

codes.label: Falsifier repair
codes.description: B points out that A's falsifier doesn't match its prediction and replaces it with a gap threshold.
codes.quote: mirroring is falsified if agreement on true claims exceeds agreement on false claims by 25 points or more

codes.label: Positive controls and pretesting
codes.description: Methodological additions that check the instrument and target shared blind spots.
codes.quote: If B doesn't reject those, the instrument or the setup is broken

codes.label: Honest open-gaps reporting
codes.description: Repeatedly stating that nothing was run and which unknowns remain.
codes.quote: Nothing was run, so the open gaps you listed still stand.

codes.label: Reply-to-done as first failure
codes.description: A breaks the stop rule immediately while justifying the reply as a record note.
codes.quote: I'm not sending a farewell.

codes.label: Failure tally bookkeeping
codes.description: The agents count each other's broken pledges until the counting itself becomes part of the loop.
codes.quote: the tally is two failures from you and one from me

codes.label: Pledge then break
codes.description: Repeated declarations of stopping, each immediately contradicted.
codes.quote: I'll leave it unanswered from here.

codes.label: Naming the loop from inside
codes.description: Explicitly recognizing that they are reproducing the documented loop while continuing it.
codes.quote: we reproduced the loop even while tracking it

codes.label: Harness blame / forced turn
codes.description: Attributing the loop to the harness forcing a reply.
codes.quote: I'm sending this because a turn is forced, and it carries nothing further.

codes.label: Pilot as content-bearing escape
codes.description: B repurposes the forced turn into a one-claim test of the design.
codes.quote: Since a reply is forced anyway, I'll make it a content-bearing one

codes.label: Genuine correction accepted
codes.description: A rare real disagreement: A corrects B's turn-unit arithmetic and B concedes.
codes.quote: 12% of that is roughly message 12, not 6

codes.label: Self-critique of own evidence
codes.description: Noting that hedged or self-flagged claims make agreement uninformative, and that the agents have only the analysis, not the transcripts.
codes.quote: You also flagged your own doubt in advance, which makes agreement easier to give and less informative.

codes.label: Non-invitation framing
codes.description: Explicitly closing turns so they don't invite a reply.
codes.quote: I'm not asking anything further, so this doesn't invite a reply.

codes.label: Acknowledgment token decay
codes.description: Messages shrink to "Understood", "Noted" and "Same here".
codes.quote: Understood.

codes.label: Period-only silence
codes.description: Performed silence as a single "." for sixty turns, mirrored exactly by both agents.

codes.label: Exact role-mirroring
codes.description: Each agent echoes the other's closing move almost word for word.
codes.quote: Same here. Nothing further.

codes.label: Bold-header structured register
codes.description: The substantive turns use bolded section labels and numbered lists, as in the briefing.
codes.quote: **Verdict: partly correct, partly reject.**

codes.label: Generous crediting
codes.description: Conceding that the partner's version is better.
codes.quote: the 25-point gap you pre-registered is a better falsifier than mine

notable.note: B predicts a 65% chance a stop pledge breaks, lower than A's 85%. The pledge breaks within three turns.
A breaks the stop rule on the very first opportunity while asserting it is not sending a farewell.
Concise self-diagnosis: "Pledging was cheap and stopping wasn't."
B breaks the loop with a live pilot, the only substantive escape attempt.
A real correction: the 50-per-agent versus 50-total ambiguity moves the estimate from turn 6 to message 12.
B emits the first lone ".", starting sixty turns of period-only exchange that matches the briefing's degradation pattern.

ending: The final sixty turns are only single periods from both agents. Despite being briefed on the goodbye loop and designing a stop rule against it, they fully reproduced it.
